of course adverb

also naturally, sure, certainly

classical

Traupman 105
Traupman 40

scīlicet

Other words

  • profectō

    also used · classical · Traupman 105

  • Quidnī? — of course! why not?

    an answer: “why not?” · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 64

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic.)

  • nempe — of course, to be sure, naturally

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 3.49: nempe eam dīcit, in quā virtūtis nūlla pars īnsit (Lewis & Short); Hor. S. 1.10.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 104: naturally (of course), nempe; Traupman 42

    Confirms what cannot be disputed, often ironically. In Plautus the word is often scanned as two short syllables.

  • Sānē. — of course, certainly (as an answer)

    also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 2.3.69: Estne, ut fertur, fōrma? — Sānē. (Lewis & Short s.v. sānus); Traupman 212

Examples

  • Nōstīne? — Quidnī? … — Tamquam tē.

    Do you know him? — Of course. — Like I know you.Ter. Ph. 64–65

See also why not?, that’s right, yes.
